title: Workspaces cannot handle updated app versions

status.label: Fix plan ready for design
status.detail: Scoop portable apps use version-specific paths removed after cleanup, breaking saved Workspaces.

next_action.label: Design stable Workspaces app paths
next_action.reason: Inspect captured path persistence and safe stable-alias resolution.

judgment.rationale: The report gives a repeatable failure and says old binaries remaining on disk mask it. A saved workspace pointing to a version-specific executable is plausible; inspect current code before choosing stable path or alias behavior.
evidence: Reporter lists Scoop portable Vivaldi, Zotero, and Foxit PDF Reader.
Failure occurs after update moves binaries and Scoop cleanup removes the old directory.
Workspace works while old binaries remain; editor later shows red X/no identity.
Reporter supplied a diagnostic ZIP and proposed shortcuts or manual paths.
judgment.recommended_action: Investigate saved executable identity/path and design stable re-resolution for portable versioned apps.

fix_assessment.rationale: The versioned-path failure is within Workspaces restore behavior and no linked public fix attempt was found; this is a focused candidate, not a confirmed implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Resolve Workspaces entries to a stable executable after app updates
proposed_fixes.root_cause: When Workspaces captures a running portable application, it likely stores the executable path inside the current version directory. Removing that directory invalidates the saved path even if a stable shortcut or alias remains.
plan: Inspect Workspaces capture, persistence, and restore paths to confirm what identity/path is saved for unpackaged apps.
On restore, resolve a stable shortcut/alias or user-configured path when the captured executable is missing; do not silently launch an unrelated PATH match.
Add tests for a versioned path changing while a stable alias points to the new version, plus an unresolved-path case.
verification: Capture a workspace with a versioned portable app, update it, remove the old version, and restore.
Verify the current alias launches the intended app, while missing or ambiguous targets are reported without launching the wrong executable.

confidence.rationale: Reporter gives a deterministic condition and says retaining the old binary masks it, implicating stale paths; restore code and safe fallback semantics remain to be confirmed.

issue_context.summary: Workspaces stops restoring portable Scoop applications after an update changes the executable directory and cleanup removes the captured old binary.
known_information: Report lists PowerToys 0.85.0 and portable apps installed through Scoop.
Reporter names Vivaldi, Zotero, and Foxit PDF Reader.
Failure follows update into a new version directory and cleanup of the old one.
Workspace works while old binaries remain; editor displays red X/no identity after cleanup.
Reporter provided a diagnostic ZIP and asks about shortcuts or manually specified paths.
inferences: Workspace capture likely persists a version-specific executable path for these unpackaged apps.
A stable alias or explicit path may permit relaunch, but safe resolution semantics need design.
issue_context.analysis: Retaining the previous binary masks the failure, supporting a stale-path explanation. Investigate path persistence; no additional generic diagnostics are needed.
initial_investigation: Read full issue and all three comments, including app names and cleanup condition.
Noted the attached report and that the prior request for logs/app names was answered.
Searched related PowerToys PRs by issue number; no linked fix found.

actions.label: Design stable Workspaces app paths
actions.note: Approve fork-side investigation of captured executable-path persistence and safe re-resolution; this does not write upstream.

actions.label: Reproduce Scoop app update path failure

reproduce.title: Restore a Workspace after a Scoop app update
prerequisites: Use a Scoop portable app whose executable path contains its version directory.
Capture a workspace while the application is running.
steps: Update the app so its executable moves to a new version directory.
Run Scoop cleanup to remove the old captured executable.
Open the saved workspace and observe whether the current executable is resolved.
Compare with a run where the old directory remains.
reproduce.expected_result: Workspaces launches the intended current executable through a stable alias/path or clearly reports no safe target; it must not silently use an obsolete or unrelated executable.
